name: City Blues: Restorativeness and Stimulating Effects of Urban Places
description: Faithful replication with the original photographs and most of the original items: nine photographs of public places in central Munich in a 3 x 3 design, place type (built, mixed, natural) x view (average place, place chosen for livability, bird's-eye view). Participants give age and gender, answer the 14-item Nature Relatedness Scale (short version used in the paper) and the matching 14-item City Relatedness Scale mixed in random order, rank the built, mixed and natural place within each view (three rankings in random order), and then rate each of the nine places in random order: whether they know the place, preference ('I like the place'), being away and fascination, the 13 new items on stimulating effects (items 1-8) and activating effects (items 9-13), and mental fatigue ('At this place, specific objects remind me of mental demands or fatigue just through their presence') with an optional note on which objects. All ratings use 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree. Rebuilt from Lämmle, von Lindern, Rummel, Michaeli & Ziegler (2022), Shedding Light onto the City Blues Myth, International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 19(13): 7606; photographs, NRS/CRS items and the 13 setting items come from its Supplementary Material (CC BY 4.0), and the per-place means computed from the authors' data file (n = 249) are stored in this template. Analysis as in the paper: mean being away, fascination, stimulating, activating, preference and mental fatigue per place; 3 x 3 repeated-measures AN(C)OVAs with nature and city relatedness as covariates (reverse-code NRS/CRS items 8, 10 and 11 before averaging); share of first, second and third ranks per place (Table S2). Differences from the original study: (1) the paper took being away and fascination from the Perceived Restorativeness Scale of Hartig, Kaiser & Bowler (1997) without printing the items; the wording here (2 being-away and 5 fascination items) is borrowed from the 16-item PRS listed in Frontiers in Public Health 10:801453; (2) the paper describes a 0-4 agreement scale but its data file is coded 1-5, which is used here; (3) the questions on enjoying nature trips and city trips are left out because their wording is not given; (4) ranking instructions and the 'know this place' question are our wording; (5) the gender options add 'other' to the paper's male/female.
author: Lämmle, von Lindern, Rummel, Michaeli & Ziegler

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. Participation is voluntary and my answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: gender
elements.title: Gender
elements.description: The paper coded male/female; 'other' is our addition.

elements.name: nrs

rows.text: I enjoy being outdoors, even in unpleasant weather.
My ideal vacation spot would be a remote, wilderness area.
I always think about how my actions affect the environment.
I enjoy digging in the earth and getting dirt on my hands.
My connection to nature and the environment is part of my spirituality.
I am very aware of environmental issues.
I take notice of wildlife wherever I am.
I don't often go out in nature.
I am not separate from nature, but part of nature.
The thought of being deep in the woods, away from civilization, is frightening.
My feelings about nature do not affect how I live my life.
Even in the middle of the city, I notice nature around me.
My relationship to nature is an important part of who I am.
I feel very connected to all living things and the earth.

elements.title: Nature Relatedness Scale
elements.description: 14 NRS items as listed in the paper's Table S4 (perspective facet not used), 1-5 agreement. Items n8, n10 and n11 are negatively worded: reverse-code before averaging.

elements.name: crs

rows.text: I like to move in the city, even in unpleasant weather.
My ideal vacation spot would be a vibrant metropolis.
I think about how to improve city life.
I like to make use of the diverse offers of the city.
My connection to the city and the city life is part of my spirituality.
I am very aware of city affairs.
I take notice of cityscape wherever I am.
I don't often go out in the city.
I am not separate from the city, but part of the city.
The thought of being in the busy, dense center of the city is frightening.
My feelings about the city do not affect how I live my life.
Even in the middle of nature, I think about the amenities in the city.
My relationship to the city is an important part of who I am.
I feel very connected to the city.

elements.title: City Relatedness Scale
elements.description: 14 CRS items from the paper's Table S4, each mirroring the NRS item with the same number, 1-5 agreement. Reverse-code c8, c10 and c11.

elements.name: rank
elements.title: Rank the three places from most to least preferred.
elements.description: Keyed by view: average, livability, bird (bird's-eye view). Value = place types in order of preference (first = most preferred).

choices.text: No, I do not know it

elements.name: preference
elements.title: I like the place.
elements.description: Single preference item, keyed by place id.

elements.name: prs

rows.text: It is an escape experience.
It gives me a good break from day-to-day routine.
The setting has fascinating qualities.
My attention is drawn to many interesting things.
I would like to get to know this place better.
There is much to explore and discover here.
I would like to spend more time looking at the surroundings.

elements.title: Perceived restorativeness: being away and fascination
elements.description: Being away = mean of ba1-ba2, fascination = mean of fa1-fa5. Borrowed wording (see description). Keyed by place id.

elements.name: setting

rows.text: This place creates a pleasant atmosphere.
This place has stimulating characteristics.
This place has a stimulating appearance.
This place invites relaxation.
In this place I recognize myself.
This place regulates my emotions in a positive sense.
This place regulates my thoughts in a positive sense.
I would meet my friends at this place, so that they can learn more about me.
This place encourages social life.
This place provides amenities.
At this place you are at the cutting edge.
This place provides a broad scope for action.
This place has something invigorating.

elements.title: Stimulating and activating effects
elements.description: 13 items from the paper's Table S5: stimulating effects = mean of s1-s8, activating effects = mean of s9-s13. Keyed by place id.

elements.name: fatigue
elements.title: At this place, specific objects remind me of mental demands or fatigue just through their presence.
elements.description: Mental fatigue item (adapted from von Lindern), keyed by place id.

elements.name: fatigue_objects
elements.title: If so, which objects?
elements.description: Optional, keyed by place id (the paper lists the answers in Table S8).
